title: The body's matter
hook: the senses, the body's life, its heat, its nourishment

segments.voice: Yesterday, rupa, matter, and the four that head its list: earth, water, fire, air, as hardness, cohesion, heat and motion. Your line: four great elements. Did a cup feel different in your hand? Day one thousand eighty-three.

A question the Abhidhamma takes seriously: what's the difference between your hand and the table it's resting on? Both, by yesterday's account, are made of the same four great elements. Both are hard, both hold together, both have a temperature, both press. Yet one of them can feel the other, and the other can't. One of them gets warm from the inside, gets hungry, heals a cut. The table does none of that. So the manual keeps going past the four, into the kinds of matter that belong only to a living body. Today, the body's matter.
screen: `YOUR HAND, AND THE TABLE.` → `THE SAME FOUR ELEMENTS.` → `ONE OF THEM FEELS.`

segments.voice: Start with the senses. In the Abhidhamma, the eye that sees is not the eyeball. It's a fine, sensitive matter inside it, ready to be struck by color. There's the same kind of sensitive matter for the ear, the nose, the tongue and the whole surface of the body. Five sensitive kinds of matter, five doors where the world gets in. A table has none, so nothing gets in. Next, life. The manual names a kind of matter it calls the life faculty, which keeps the other kinds of living matter going, the way a caretaker keeps a garden watered. When it stops, the four great elements are still there, but the body is no longer alive. Then heat. Yesterday fire was simply temperature. Here the manual adds that temperature is one of the forces that keeps producing matter, moment after moment: warmth in a living body isn't just a reading on a thermometer, it's part of what keeps the body being made. And then nourishment. Food, in this system, carries a subtle nutritive essence, and that essence too keeps producing matter in the body. So the manual names four things that keep matter arising: past kamma, the mind, temperature and food. A table gets only one of those. A living body gets all four. Notice what the list does not do. It never adds a fifth thing, a soul or a self, to explain the difference. A living body is matter held up by more conditions, not matter with someone hiding inside it. In one sutta the Buddha says that the world, its arising and its ending are found in this fathom-long body, with its perception and mind. The Abhidhamma takes him at his word and starts measuring.
screen: `FIVE SENSITIVE DOORS.` · `THE LIFE FACULTY KEEPS IT GOING.` · `HEAT AND FOOD KEEP MAKING MATTER.` · then, large: `NO ONE HIDING INSIDE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: feel your body's warmth. Settle, and bring your attention to your hands. Notice their temperature, without deciding whether it's pleasant. Then let attention move to the belly, to the chest, to the back of the neck. Somewhere, there's warmth. Rest there. That warmth is the body doing its work, moment by moment, without your help. If you like, place one palm over the other and feel heat meeting heat. The bell holds the time.
The body's matter. The sense doors, the life faculty, and the heat and food that keep a living body being made. Today's word.
Your line: living matter. Today, at your next meal, feel the warmth of your hands before you eat and again after, and remember what the manual says food is doing. Day one thousand eighty-three.

howItsDone: Abhidhamma students learn the kinds of matter found only in living bodies, such as the sense organs' sensitive matter and the life faculty, and some meditation teachers in the Theravada tradition guide students to feel warmth and other qualities in the body directly.

myth: in the Abhidhamma, the eye that sees is the eyeball
it's a fine, sensitive matter inside the eye, ready to be struck by color.
the manual names kamma, mind, temperature and food as producers of matter
a living body gets all four; a table gets only one.
the manual adds a soul to explain why a body is alive

fork.setup: a living hand and a table are both made of the four great elements. what does the manual say makes the difference?
options: a self hiding in the hand
more kinds of matter and more conditions: sense doors, life, heat, food
fork.reveal: the manual lists sensitive matter, the life faculty, and matter kept arising by kamma, mind, temperature and food. it never adds a self.

original.note: Pali: the life faculty, the kind of matter that keeps the other living matter going.

trapdoor: what you thought: the body is just flesh and bones.
what it means: a body is the four elements plus sense doors, life, and matter kept arising by heat and food.
what a scholar hears: the manual names four producers of matter, kamma, mind, temperature and nutriment, and adds no self.
recall: a factor that colors the knowing

sources.ref: Abhidhammattha Sangaha VI (Compendium of Matter), sensitive matter, life faculty, the four origins of matter

notes: Five sensitive kinds of matter (pasada rupa) and the life faculty (jivitindriya) as listed in Abhidhammattha Sangaha VI; confirm.
The caretaker/garden simile for the life faculty is the writer's own image; the Visuddhimagga's simile (water maintaining lotuses, or a ferryman) may be preferred by a Keeper.
'Heat' here is temperature (utu) as one of the four producers of matter; the index's 'its heat' might also be read as the digestive fire. Confirm framing.
Four origins of matter (kamma, citta, utu, ahara) per Sangaha VI; 'a table gets only one' (temperature-born matter) is the standard reading for external matter; confirm.
AN 4.45 (Rohitassa) is paraphrased; confirm the reference and wording.
Original: Devanagari spelling of jivitindriya; confirm.
Editor pass: the carry no longer tells the listener that warmth will come back after eating; it invites them to check before and after.
